eligibility.evidence: Sec 3 and 4.1-4.3 (pp. 6-15): ChatGPT (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4-1106) is the participant in three replications of published human experiments (Goel et al. 2017 gain/loss framing and contextualisation; Lee et al. 2018 perspective-taking; Nuijten et al. 2016 deaf effect); cites the human studies (E2 test a) and Tversky & Kahneman 1981. New responses and regression outcomes (E1, E3, E4). N=880 model outputs.

D.metric: Qualitative comparison of direction and significance with the findings of the three original studies; no human data are analysed in this paper

effects.model: ChatGPT (Study 1; version not stated, pooled across 3 Oct and 10 Nov 2023 runs)
effects.label: SAME-DIRECTION-UNQUANTIFIED
effects.location: Sec 4.1 pp.9-11, Fig 3, Table 1 (M1-M3, p.10). Human-role (student) condition used as the human proxy; authors state frame and context effects appear for student role not AI. Table 1 signs for Framing (Loss=1 +0.48) do not obviously match that text; Context (High=1) B=-1.36, p<0.001 pooled across roles. Original findings: Goel et al. as summarised on p.10.

effects.model: GPT-4 and GPT-4-1106 preview (pooled, model as covariate)
effects.label: SAME-DIRECTION-UNQUANTIFIED
effects.location: Sec 4.2 pp.11-13, Fig 4, Table 2 (M1-M3, p.12): perspective effect on launch decision B=-2.08 (SE 0.18, p<0.001) and on guilt B=+2.78 (p<0.001) in reference (human-role) condition, with the table's coding label reversed against the text; Role x Perspective interaction significant. Sec 5.1 p.15 'resonating with' Lee et al. 2018.

effects.label: SAME-DIRECTION-UNQUANTIFIED
effects.location: Sec 4.3 pp.13-15, Fig 5, Table 3 (M1-M6, p.15): perceived control (High=1) raises continuation (B about 2.4 to 3.2, p<0.001); 'similar to human participants' (p.14). Messenger main effect not significant in M1 (p=0.338); messenger effect depends on GPT role.

E.headline: Prompted as a human, ChatGPT shows human-like susceptibility to framing, perspective and control manipulations; prompted as AI, it is more consistent and less biased.

G.notes: Regression tables are garbled in conversion and coding labels look inconsistent with the text (Table 2 perspective sign; Sec 4.1 framing text against Table 1; Sec 5.1 says role effects larger for AI, Sec 4.2 says smaller). Study 1 model and GPT-3.5 use unstated. Human comparison is qualitative only. No code or data link.
